item.title: Health PEI Launches new Applicant Tracking System
item.description:
Health PEI Launches new Applicant Tracking System jpranahan Fri, 11/06/2026 - 11:52

Health PEI has recently launched a new applicant tracking system (ATS), providing a more streamlined and user-friendly experience for individuals interested in health care careers across Prince Edward Island.

The new system makes it easier for candidates to search, filter, and apply for opportunities with Health PEI. The platform features a simplified application process, mobile-friendly design, and bilingual access in both English and French.

Applicants can create and manage a personal profile, apply to multiple job opportunities, track the status of their applications, and sign up for job alerts based on their areas of interest.

"Attracting and recruiting talented health care professionals is essential to strengthening our health system and improving access to care for Islanders. This new applicant tracking system modernizes the recruitment experience, making it easier for people to explore career opportunities, connect with Health PEI, and contribute to the delivery of health care across the province."

-  Minister of Health and Wellness, Cory Deagle

In addition to improving the candidate and employee experience, the platform also strengthens workforce planning by capturing key recruitment data, including application volumes, internal workforce trends, candidate qualifications, and time-to-hire metrics. 

"The applicant tracking system represents an important step forward in our efforts to attract and hire the health care professionals our province needs," said Pico Sine, Director of Workforce Recruitment with Health PEI. "By providing a simple and more accessible application experience, we’re making it easier for candidates to connect with job opportunities and for employees to grow their careers across our health care system.”

The launch of the new system is part of Health PEI's efforts to modernize recruitment processes and improve access for job seekers interested in building a health care career on Prince Edward Island.

Individuals interested in exploring career opportunities with Health PEI can visit Health PEI Jobs | JobsPEI to create a profile, sign up for job alerts, and apply for current opportunities.

item.title: Premier Lantz recognizes National Indigenous Veterans Day
item.description:
Premier Lantz recognizes National Indigenous Veterans Day jpranahan Fri, 11/06/2026 - 11:17

Premier Rob Lantz issued the following statement recognizing National Indigenous Veterans Day on November 8:

“Today, we honour the First Nations, Inuit and Métis men and women who have served Canada with courage and dedication.

For generations, Indigenous people have answered the call to serve—from the world wars to peacekeeping missions and military operations around the world.

Yet despite their service and sacrifice, many Indigenous veterans returned home to discrimination and were denied benefits and opportunities afforded to other veterans. This injustice is an important part of our country’s history, and it must not be overlooked.

Here on Prince Edward Island, we honour the service of Mi’kmaw veterans and recognize the lasting impact of their sacrifices on their families and communities.

National Indigenous Veterans Day is a time to remember those who lost their lives, honour those who returned home and recognize the generations of Indigenous families who have supported those who serve.

We owe it to these veterans and to future generations to preserve their stories, and ensure their contributions are never forgotten.

Lest we forget.”

item.title: Rural transit marks five years of serving Islanders
item.description:
Rural transit marks five years of serving Islanders jpranahan Thu, 11/05/2026 - 14:26

For the past five years, rural transit has helped Islanders get where they need to go by providing an affordable and reliable transportation option.

During that time, it has become an established part of the province’s transportation network by connecting rural communities with larger centres and making it easier for Islanders to access work, services and everyday needs.

“Over the past five years, rural transit has made a real difference for people in communities across PEI,” said Transportation and Infrastructure Minister Bloyce Thompson. “This milestone reflects the tremendous growth of the service, and we look forward to continuing to enhance it for Islanders in the years ahead.”

The provincial government recently signed a five-year agreement with Trius Transit to continue the rural transit service, giving it further stability and a stronger foundation for continued improvements. This supports the province’s commitment to safe, affordable, and sustainable transportation for Islanders.

“Affordability for people has been a cornerstone of rural transit,” Minister Thompson added. “Offering $2 one-way fare, low cost monthly passes and free travel for children and students from kindergarten to Grade 12, makes this a very valuable service for many Islanders.”

The next phase will focus on providing reliable, accessible service, with enough capacity to meet demand and improvements based on ridership trends and community feedback. 

“Rural transit can make a real difference in people’s lives,” said Trius Transit president Matthew Cassidy. “As we mark five years of this service on PEI, we’re proud to make transportation more accessible, convenient and affordable for Islanders.”

To accommodate growing ridership, larger motorcoach buses have been added to the Western PEI, Three Rivers and Montague routes, offering more seating and improved comfort for passengers.

Quick facts:

  • More than 550,000 one-way passenger trips have been taken since 2021. 
  • Rural transit has grown from three to eight year-round routes and services from Tignish to Souris. 
  • Monthly ridership has grown from about 1,500 trips in 2021 to almost 13,000 trips in 2026. 
  • Rural transit recorded 15,376 one-way trips in September 2026, the third-highest monthly total on record. 
  • Ridership reached 115,948 trips between January and September 2026, five per cent higher than during the same period in 2025. 
  • The North Shore summer shuttle provided more than 11,000 one-way trips in 2026.

For more information on schedules or to book a seat, visit the Trius Transit website.

item.title: New cyberviolence prevention grants support community-led initiatives
item.description:
New cyberviolence prevention grants support community-led initiatives jenniferdhogan Wed, 11/04/2026 - 15:15

Seven community organizations are receiving provincial funding from the new Cyberviolence Prevention Grant to help young Islanders build safer and more respectful online communities. 

Through the Interministerial Women's Secretariat, the province is investing $100,000 in community-led initiatives that will help young people develop the skills and confidence they need to navigate digital spaces safely. The initiative is a key action under Prince Edward Island's Youth Cyberviolence Prevention Strategy and will support projects designed to prevent cyberbullying, promote healthy online behaviour and increase awareness of cyberviolence among youth.

"Digital spaces are an important part of everyday life for young people, offering opportunities to learn, connect and express themselves. These community-led projects will help equip young Islanders with the knowledge and tools they need to stay safe online while fostering a culture of respect, inclusion and kindness in digital spaces."

- Minister of Workforce and Advanced Learning and Minister responsible for the Status of Women, Jenn Redmond.

The grant program was developed in response to feedback gathered during consultations for the Youth Cyberviolence Prevention Strategy. Young people, parents, caregivers and community partners identified the need for stronger support, practical resources and greater awareness to address cyberviolence and its impacts.

More than half of parents and caregivers surveyed during the strategy's development reported that a young person in their care had experienced some form of cyberviolence. Funded projects include cyberbullying prevention, digital citizenship education, youth leadership development, and resources tailored to newcomer youth, LGBTQIA+ youth, and young people with learning disabilities. 

“With this grant, STEAM PEI and the PEI IT Alliance are working together hosting Cyber Titans, a program to empower young Islanders with the knowledge, skills, and confidence they need to thrive in an increasingly digital world,” said STEAM PEI director of partnership and development Emily Wood. “These learning opportunities will promote healthy online behaviours by allowing youth to develop the skills to recognize online vulnerabilities, understand the impact of their digital interactions, and make informed choices that contribute to safer, more respectful, and inclusive online communities across the Island.”

For more information on the Provincial Youth Cyberviolence Prevent Strategy and resources on cyber safety, visit cybersafecarepei.ca. 

 

Media contact:
April Gallant
Department of Workforce and Advanced Learning
aldgallant@gov.pe.ca

 

Backgrounder: 

Cyberviolence Prevention Grant Recipients 2026

Learning Disabilities Association of PEI; for their project: Cyber Violence Prevention for those with Learning Disabilities, a project that will enhance awareness, education, and action toward preventing cyberviolence in Prince Edward Island by delivering targeted, accessible training and resources focused on youth with learning disabilities.

Amount: $8,000

Chinese Society of PEI: for their project, Safe Screens PEI: Chinese Youth Against Cyberviolence; a six-month bilingual prevention project for Chinese, immigrant, racialized and linguistically diverse youth in PEI, with priority for girls and young women.

Amount: $10,000

PEERS Alliance; for their project: Building Resillience: An Anti Cyber violence campaign, where workshops will be developed for various demographics within the LGBTQIA+ Demographic and be presented to various focus groups with both organizations and community members to gain a broader understanding of the specific kinds of rhetoric individuals are being subjected to.

Amount: $15,000

Sport PEI: for their project; Play with Respect. Post with Respect, where SPORT PEI will create a province-wide awareness campaign and host Community Engagement Activations promoting positive digital cultures and encourage respectful online behavior. The project will also develop a Digital Playbook, providing tips on communication best practices, platform guidance, sample templates, reporting information and educational resources for athletes, coaches, officials, volunteers and families.

Amount: $15,000

Community Legal Information Association of Prince Edward Island: for their project Earlier Education, Stronger Prevention: Expanding Cyberbullying Intervention; a project that will create an interactive, trauma-informed, and age-appropriate educational resource for PEI youth aged 10-11 and deliver the pilot workshop meeting the Health & Phys Ed. curriculum outcomes for grades 5-6.

Amount: $17,250

East Prince Women’s Information Centre (EPWIC): for their project, Youth Creating Healthy Digital Spaces & Culture, where EPWIC and Generation XX will create a Youth Digital Leadership Team and Speakers Bureau in response to PEI’s Provincial Youth Cyberviolence Prevention Strategy.

Amount: $17,250

S.T.E.A.M. PEI: for their project, Cyber Titans. Cyber Titans in partnership with the PEI IT Alliance which will empower PEI youth to prevent cyberviolence by building the knowledge, skills, and ethical foundation needed to become responsible digital citizens. The program combines hands-on cybersecurity training with education on cyber ethics, online safety, cyberbullying, harassment, image-based abuse, and the consequences of harmful online behaviour.

Amount: $17,500

item.title: New measures continue to improve safety in Island schools
item.description:
New measures continue to improve safety in Island schools jenniferdhogan Wed, 11/04/2026 - 14:30

Safety at Island schools remains a top priority as government continues to act on recommendations made by former Chief Justice of the Prince Edward Island Court of Appeal David Jenkins.

In his report titled Student Safety in Island Schools: Handling of Complaints and Incidents of Staff Sexual Misconduct (the Jenkins Report), the former Chief Justice made more than 60 recommendations for the Department of Education and Early Years, the Public Schools Branch (PSB), La Commission scolaire de langue française (CSLF), and other government departments. The report, commissioned in May 2025 after two serious student safety incidents, identified vulnerabilities in existing safeguards and recommended improvements and measures to better protect children in Island schools.

“The department and the education authorities have done tremendous work in their response to the Jenkins report, and I commend them for their efforts to improve safety for students and staff. There is still work to be done, but I am pleased with the progress thus far and I look forward to seeing even more recommendations implemented in the near future.” 

- Minister of Education and Early Years Robin Croucher

Of the 62 recommendations in the report 50 have been acted on including the implementation of the following measures:

  • A new stand-alone sexual misconduct policy, which has been approved by the PSB and CSLF
  • An enhanced incident reporting system that can better identify trends and track incidents
  • Mandatory annual training and refresher training for staff on recognizing and preventing child sexual abuse
  • Enhanced criminal record and vulnerable sector checks
  • Better coordination between Child Protection Services, law enforcement, the Department of Education and Early Years, and the Child & Youth Advocate to close information gaps
  • Internal procedures to ensure incident reports reach the right department and are acted on without delay
  • Annual offense declarations for all staff, including immediate disclosure of new offenses
  • Training on Duty to Report and the legal requirement to report incidents to law enforcement and or Child Protective Services immediately

Work continues to address another 11 recommendations including:

  • Development of a new code of conduct for Island schools that will set out expectations for staff, students, parents and guardians, and volunteers 
  • Alignment of the Safe & Caring Learning Environment policy with the new sexual misconduct policy
  • Changes to legislation to align the Education Act, The Child and Family Services Act, and the new sexual misconduct policy.

To view the full report, visit Student Safety in Island Schools

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
